info.bio:
Temple of the Dog, a pesar de haber publicado sólo un álbum, es una de las bandas más representativas del movimiento grunge de principios de los noventa.

Temple of the Dog fue creada por Chris Cornell, como tributo al vocalista de Mother Love Bone, Andrew Wood, fallecido por una sobredosis de estupefacientes.

La banda estuvo conformada por los anteriores miembros de Mother Love Bone, el guitarrista Stone Gossard y el bajista Jeff Ament,sumados al cantante Chris Cornell

scenes.name: Grunge
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: Andrew Wood Memorial
podcast.body: Temple of the Dog was a Seattle supergroup formed specifically to record an album in memory of Andrew Wood, the singer of Mother Love Bone, who died of a heroin overdose. The project brought together surviving members of Mother Love Bone and friends from Soundgarden. "Some of the surviving members of Mother Love Bone got together with friends from Soundgarden, a few other local musicians to record an album in Andrew's memory. They called their Seattle group Temple of the Dog."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Catalyst for Pearl Jam
podcast.body: The musicians who participated in the Temple of the Dog recording sessions enjoyed their time together, leading Mother Love Bone's bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard to decide to continue working together, eventually forming Pearl Jam with Mike McCready and Eddie Vedder. "Most of the musicians who took part in the Temple of the Dog Sessions really had a good time hanging out. And when the record was finished, Mother Love Bone's bassist and guitarist decided to stick together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation as a Tribute
podcast.body: Temple of the Dog was formed as a one-time-only band specifically as a tribute to Andrew Wood, who was Chris Cornell's roommate and a member of Mother Love Bone. "And as a tribute, he formed a one-time only band called Temple of the Dog."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Impact of Andrew Wood's Death
podcast.body: The formation of Temple of the Dog and subsequently Pearl Jam raises questions about whether these collaborations would have occurred had it not been for Andrew Wood's untimely death. "So it makes you wonder if they would have ever come together, but not been for Andrew's death."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Initial Lack of Attention, Later Multi-Platinum Success – Post-Hype Phenomenon
podcast.body: Despite receiving great reviews upon its release in April 1991, the Temple of the Dog album was largely ignored by the public. However, once Mookie Blaylock changed its name to Pearl Jam and both Soundgarden and Pearl Jam achieved massive global success, interest in the album exploded, leading it to sell multi-platinum worldwide. "It got great reviews, but nobody paid much attention until Mookie Blaylock changed their name to Pearl Jam and, well, you know, that story."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Members' Future Bands
podcast.body: After the Temple of the Dog album was released, Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron were active in Soundgarden, while Stone Gossard, Jeff Ament, Mike McCready, and Eddie Vedder formed Pearl Jam. "By the time that Temple of Dog album came out, Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron were doing well in Soundgarden, while the other guys in the group stayed together in Formed Pearl Jam."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Seattle Grunge Supergroup
podcast.body: The project is considered, in retrospect, a Seattle Grunge Supergroup, combining members who were already established in Soundgarden with others who would go on to form Pearl Jam. "Temple of the Dog, what in retrospect is a Seattle Grunge Supergroup featuring members of Soundgarden and future members of Pearl Jam."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tribute to Andrew Wood
podcast.body: The band formed to record a tribute album for Andrew Wood, the deceased singer of Mother Love Bone, an event crucial to the coalescence of the Seattle grunge scene. "Some of his friends came together to record a tribute album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tribute to Andrew Wood
podcast.body: Temple of the Dog was formed as a quick tribute to Andrew Wood, Chris Cornell's former roommate and the singer of Mother Love Bone, who tragically died in March 1990. Cornell wrote several songs in his friend's honor, which he then shared with the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, leading to the formation of this supergroup. "When he got back to Seattle, he showed the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, the songs. When other materials started flowing, they decided to record a quick tribute album under the name Temple of the Dog."

xref.title: Performance with Chester Bennington (2008)
xref.body: During the 2008 Project Revolution Tour, Chris Cornell was performing when Chester Bennington unexpectedly joined him on stage to sing "Hunger Strike." This Temple of the Dog song was written by Cornell as a tribute to his late roommate, Andrew Wood of Mother Lovevont. "If we go back to the 2008 project revolution tour, Chris was on the bill. And when he stepped forward to sing the Temple of Dog Song, Hunger Strike, a song written for and dedicated to Chris's late roommate Andrew Wood of Mother Lovevont, Chester surprised everybody by coming in to sing with him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Death
xref.body: Lead singer Andrew Wood overdosed on heroin, suffered a massive cerebral hemorrhage, and died just before the release of their debut album, "Apple." His death was a crucial event that set in motion the formation of other bands and projects like Temple of the Dog, contributing to the scene's coalescence. "Not just before that album was released, their singer Andrew Wood, overdosed on heroin, suffered a massive cerebral hemorrhage, and died."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andrew Wood's Roommate at Time of Death
xref.body: Chris Cornell was Andrew Wood's roommate at the time of his death, a detail that ties into the formation of Temple of the Dog as a tribute. "Andrew's roommate at the time he died was Chris Cornell."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation from Mother Love Bone and Temple of the Dog
xref.body: Pearl Jam was formed by Mother Love Bone's bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard, who decided to continue playing together after the Temple of the Dog sessions. They were joined by guitarist Mike McCready, a veteran of several small Seattle groups, and singer Eddie Vedder, who had moved from San Diego to perform background vocals on the Temple of the Dog record. "Jeff Ammett and Stone Gossard were joined by guitarist Mike McCready, a veteran of several small Seattle groups. And for a singer, they chose this skinny surfer dude who had moved up from San Diego to do background vocals on the Temple of the Dog record. His name was Eddie Vetter and the result of course was Pearl Jam."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Legacy and Band Spin-offs
xref.body: Following Andrew Wood's death, the surviving members, bassist Jeff Ament and guitarist Stone Gossard, along with friends from Soundgarden, formed Temple of the Dog to record a memorial album. The positive experience of these sessions eventually led Ament and Gossard to form Pearl Jam. "Some of the surviving members of Mother Love Bone got together with friends from Soundgarden, a few other local musicians to record an album in Andrew's memory."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Major Label Reputation Building
xref.body: By the time the Temple of the Dog album was released, Soundgarden was actively building their reputation, having already secured a new major label record deal. "Soundgarden was well into building their reputation with a new major label record deal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Temple of the Dog Rise – Boosts Prior Project
xref.body: After Mookie Blaylock changed their name to Pearl Jam and the band "blew up," their success retrospectively drew massive attention to the Temple of the Dog album, which had initially been ignored. This surge in popularity led the Temple of the Dog record to achieve multi-platinum sales worldwide. "But when Soundgarden and Pearl Jam blew up, the record went multi-platinum all over the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Roommate of Andrew Wood – Impact on Temple of the Dog
xref.body: Chris Cornell shared an apartment with Andrew Wood, the singer of Mother Love Bone. Wood's unexpected death in March 1990 profoundly affected Cornell, leading him to write songs in tribute that eventually formed the basis of the Temple of the Dog project. "Andrew died the day Chris got back from a long tour with Soundgarden. A few days after the funeral, Chris and Soundgarden headed out on a European tour, and while on the road, Chris started running some songs in tribute to his old friend."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Temple of the Dog Collaboration
xref.body: Following the death of Andrew Wood from Mother Love Bone, members of Soundgarden joined surviving Mother Love Bone members and other local musicians to record an album in Wood's memory, forming the supergroup Temple of the Dog. "Some of the surviving members of Mother Love Bone got together with friends from Soundgarden, a few other local musicians to record an album in Andrew's memory."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tragic Death of Andrew Wood
xref.body: Three weeks before the scheduled release of their debut album, "Apple," Mother Love Bone's singer Andrew Wood died from a heroin overdose. This tragedy led to the formation of Temple of the Dog as a tribute and subsequently, Pearl Jam. "Three weeks before it comes out, singer Andrew Wood dies of a heroin overdose."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Transformation into Pearl Jam – Post-Tragedy Rebirth
xref.body: Following the tragic death of Andrew Wood, the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard, collaborated with Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron to form Temple of the Dog. This collaboration eventually led Ament and Gossard to form a new band with Eddie Vedder, initially called Mookie Blaylock, which soon became Pearl Jam. "When Mother Lovebone collapsed and turned into Pearl Jam, Kelly became their full-time manager, leaving Susan to deal with Allison Chains."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
